key_insight: TRCGL-Net combines tail-class synthetic image generation with feature, attention, and label-co-occurrence modeling to improve rare-disease chest X-ray classification in long-tailed multi-label settings.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help computer-aided chest X-ray systems recognize uncommon findings more reliably, supporting more balanced model performance across common and rare conditions.
method: Text-guided conditional diffusion generates semantically constrained synthetic tail-class chest X-rays.
Channel reweighting and class-aware attention emphasize disease-relevant features and lesion regions.
Graph convolution models label co-occurrence to propagate information across diagnoses.
evidence_signal: On the PadChest dataset, the method reported tail-class mAP of 0.4904, overall mAP of 0.4408, and mAUC of 0.8989, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines.
watch_item: Synthetic data and co-occurrence modeling can improve performance, but real-world robustness still depends on careful validation across hospitals, scanners, and label quality.
paper_title: TRCGL-Net: A Long-Tailed Multi-Label Chest X-Ray Classification Framework with Generative Data Augmentation and Label Co-Occurrence Modeling
